title: quantization-nan-debug-scratchpad-lee-2026-04-20
content:
Purpose:
Quick scratchpad for the NaN / quality regression we've been seeing after applying INT8/FP8 quantization profiles to the 'redwood-chat-medium' family. Notes here are messy — steps tried, log snippets, hypotheses, next actions.

Summary of problem:
- After switching to the new FP8 quantization profile (fp8-e4m3 hybrid for activations, per-channel int8 for weights), some prompts generate NaNs in the KV cache, which then propagate and result in all-NaN logits for some batches.
- Behavior appears intermittent: reproduces ~1/5 runs on the same checkpoint on A100. Higher sequence lengths and multi-turn prompts increase probability.
- BF16 runs are fine. INT8-only profile also shows occasional quality drop but not NaNs. FP8 hybrid seems to trigger NaNs more reliably.

Commands / repro attempts tried:
1) Basic repro script (single GPU):
python tools/run_inference.py --model models/redwood-chat-medium.fp8-profile --quantize fp8 --batch-size 1 --input tests/long_prompt.txt --seq-len 512 --seed 42 --device cuda:0
-> Observed NaN in logits at token 117 sometimes.

2) Deterministic seed + repeat to capture flakiness:
for i in {1..20}; do python tools/run_inference.py --model models/redwood-chat-medium.fp8-profile --quantize fp8 --batch-size 1 --input tests/long_prompt.txt --seq-len 512 --seed 42; done
-> Reproduced NaN on runs 3, 8, 12. Not consistent.

3) Increase FP8 mantissa precision (temporary flag):
python tools/run_inference.py --model ... --quantize fp8 --fp8-mantissa-bits 4
-> Reduced frequency but not eliminated.

4) Run on CPU fallback (no GPU kernels) to see if it's kernel-related:
python tools/run_inference.py --device cpu --model models/redwood-chat-medium.fp8-profile --quantize fp8
-> No NaNs observed (but much slower). Suggests kernel/hardware path issue or GPU-specific cast behavior.

5) Run with KV cache disabled (force recompute):
python tools/run_inference.py --model ... --quantize fp8 --disable-kv-cache
-> No NaNs. Points to KV cache update path as culprit (write/read of cached tensors).

6) Instrumented run printing max/min of tensors in attention update loop (cuda:synchronized): added checks at end of each step:
  if torch.isnan(x).any(): print(f"NaN detected step {step}")
  print(step, x.min().item(), x.max().item(), x.abs().max().item())
-> NaNs appear immediately after kv_cache write+read for some heads. Pre-write values look finite, post-read contain NaN.

Error snippets / logs:
- CUDA kernel log captured in debug mode:
[W] kernel_check: atomicAdd overflow? returning INF
[ERROR] aten::mul_cuda kernel crashed: nan encountered in output
Traceback (most recent calls...): RuntimeError: CUDA error: device-side assert triggered

- Torch NaN detection snippet:
Step 116: attn_out min=-1.234, max=2.98, abs_max=2.98
Step 117: attn_out min=nan, max=nan, abs_max=nan  <-- first NaN

Hypotheses (ranked):
1) KV cache read/write alignment / dtype cast bug in FP8 path for attention keys/values. FP8 quantization + compression packing/unpacking may not align per-head in edge cases (seq len mod block size).
2) Accumulation overflow in fused attention kernel when casting from FP8->FP32 for softmax with large negative logits causing NaN after subtract+exp underflow/overflow in fp8 path.
3) Race condition in async kernel path causing uninitialized memory to be read (GPU only, because CPU runs are fine).
4) Model weights or per-channel scales include NaNs due to a bad quantization calibration on some channels (less likely because BF16/INT8 non-NaN).

Quick checks that support hypotheses:
- Disabling KV cache (recompute path) removes issue -> implicates cache write/read serialization/packing.
- CPU no-NaN -> implicates GPU kernels or CUDA-specific quant/cast behavior.
- Increasing FP8 mantissa reduced frequency -> suggests precision/rounding sensitivity contributing.
- Running with seq-len 128 rarely reproduces; seq-len >=512 reproduces more -> maybe block-buffering issue.

Bisect / next repro steps planned:
- Add deterministic per-step memfill check before reading KV cache to catch uninitialized reads (write a sentinel pattern immediately after packing).
- Force synchronous kernel launches around KV write/read to see if race goes away: set TORCH_CUDA_LAUNCH_BLOCKING=1 and rerun 50x.
- Instrument the pack/unpack code to dump raw bytes for the head/block that goes NaN and compare good vs bad runs (hex dump).
- Add extra sanity checks in quantize/dequantize: clamp values, check scales not zero/inf/nan before pack.
- Re-run failing case under cuda-memcheck to see if there is illegal memory access.

Temporary mitigations tried:
- Fallback to BF16 profile for affected customers (works).
- When running FP8, apply an extra post-read clamp: replace NaNs in KV cache with zeros and log occurrence. This avoids crash but likely degrades quality.

Notes for deeper kernel debugging:
- Candidate file: runtime/kernels/attention_fp8.cu (pack/unpack routines) - line ~420 pack_kv_blocks() suspected.
- Another suspect: runtime/quantization/fp8_packer.cu (alignment math for per-channel blocks).
- Related PR that changed block size behavior: PR #652 (see linked PR 678 for later tweaks).

Repro artifacts to capture (TODO):
- small tarball with model weights, calibration tables, and failing input prompt + seed
- verbose cuda kernel trace (NVIDIA Nsight or cuda-gdb log)
- hex dumps of packed KV for failing head

Immediate actions (this week):
- (Lee) add sentinel memfill after pack() and enable TORCH_CUDA_LAUNCH_BLOCKING for 100 runs, capture frequency (ETA 1 day)
- (Maya) add nan/inf checks in quant pack/unpack and add clamping with warning logs (ETA 2 days)
- (Nate) run cuda-memcheck + asan on kernels in CI matrix for A100 (ETA 3 days)

Open questions:
- Does pack() assume 64 byte alignment for blocks? What happens when seq_len%block_size != 0?
- Are there platform-specific cuBLAS/cuDNN fused kernels that behave differently for e4m3 vs e5m2 FP8 encodings?
- Can we publish a minimal reproducer that triggers NaN in isolation (no model)?

If this turns out to be a race/uninitialized memory bug in our packing code, it's high priority (can cause silent corruption). If it's numeric overflow due to fp8 accumulation, then we need to re-evaluate accumulation datatype (FP32 accumulation vs FP16) and possibly adjust softmax pre-scaling/clamping.

Bottom line: evidence currently points to a GPU kernel/path issue around KV cache pack/unpack in the FP8 hybrid profile. Next step is to gather deterministic traces and add defensive checks to facilitate root cause isolation.

Scratchpad notes:
- observed non-determinism seems higher when Multi-GPU/NCCL is active -> maybe stale pointer from peer access
- try run with --no-persistent-cuda-memory in case of allocator reuse bug
- test with different CUDA versions (12.1 vs 12.3) on CI reproducer

End of scratchpad.
